jobDescription: A card-issuing fintech processes authorisations for prepaid and credit cards on behalf of partner brands. Its site reliability engineers run the authorisation services on Kubernetes with infrastructure as code, set and defend service-level objectives, prepare the platform for seasonal peaks, and take turns as incident commander whenever a severity-1 incident is declared. Engineers are also expected to help newer colleagues become safe and confident on call. Authorisation volumes roughly triple between late November and early January, and the card schemes require every severity-1 incident to be reported with a timeline and root cause within five working days, so incident records are kept carefully.
requirements: Operates card-authorisation services on Kubernetes with infrastructure defined as code.
Acts as incident commander for severity-1 incidents and runs the incident bridge.
Defines service-level objectives and alerting for authorisation availability and latency.
Automates capacity tests ahead of peak trading periods.
Mentors junior engineers on reliability practice and on-call readiness.

evidence.text: Site reliability engineer at Quayline Cards (prepaid and credit card issuer), August 2020 to present; ran the card-authorisation services on Kubernetes with cluster and network configuration managed in Terraform.
Defined the 99.95% availability and 300-millisecond p99 latency objectives for authorisation and set burn-rate alerts that page the on-call engineer.
Built the capacity-test pipeline that replays a scaled copy of the previous Black Friday's authorisation traffic against a pre-production cluster every October.
Moved certificate rotation for the card-network connections from a manual quarterly task to a scheduled job with expiry alerts.
Paired with two graduate engineers during their first on-call month and reviewed their runbook changes.

Work sample: the SLO definition page for the authorisation service, showing the availability and latency objectives, the error-budget policy and the alert thresholds, with the change record that approved it.

Reference check summary: the former head of platform engineering confirmed in writing that the candidate acted as incident commander for seven severity-1 authorisation incidents between May 2022 and June 2024, and supplied the incident log entries that name the candidate in that role.
Background screening result: employment dates at Quayline Cards (August 2020 to present) were confirmed by the employer's HR team through the employment verification service.
